#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Detect whether NVIDIA drives the display (rather than a hybrid iGPU).

# On hybrid laptops the display is usually wired to the integrated GPU while
# the NVIDIA card only handles offloaded rendering. Forcing NVIDIA's VA-API and
# GLX drivers globally then breaks Chromium-based browsers (black video with
# audio still playing), so the Hyprland NVIDIA env only applies when NVIDIA is
# the display GPU.
#
# sysfs exposes which VGA device drives the display via boot_vga. When no
# device claims it (attribute missing or unreadable), assume NVIDIA is the
# display GPU to preserve the current behavior on machines we cannot tell.
#
# Read the cached sysfs IDs rather than lspci, which reads PCI config space and
# resumes runtime-suspended GPUs.
pci_devices_path="${OMARCHY_PCI_DEVICES_PATH:-/sys/bus/pci/devices}"

shopt -s nullglob

nvidia_boot=0
other_boot=0

for device in "$pci_devices_path"/*; do
  [[ $(< "$device/class") == 0x03* ]] || continue
  boot_vga=0
  if [[ -f $device/boot_vga ]]; then
    boot_vga=$(< "$device/boot_vga")
  fi
  if [[ $(< "$device/vendor") == "0x10de" ]]; then
    if (( boot_vga == 1 )); then
      nvidia_boot=1
    fi
  else
    if (( boot_vga == 1 )); then
      other_boot=1
    fi
  fi
done

if (( other_boot == 1 && nvidia_boot == 0 )); then
  exit 1
else
  exit 0
fi

#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Returns true when the compositor holds a session lock no other locker is alive to own
# omarchy:args=<own-pid>
# omarchy:hidden=true

# Hyprland lets any client take over a held lock (misc:allow_session_lock_restore),
# so a shell that recovers a lock it merely sees can take the live lock screen of
# another shell, and strand it when it exits. A lock is stranded only while no
# other Quickshell or hyprlock is running; until then the answer is undetermined,
# so the caller keeps asking until that locker exits or it gives up.
#
# Exits 0 stranded, 1 unlocked, 2 undetermined. The caller passes its own pid,
# as a crash re-execs the shell in place.
omarchy-hyprland-session-locked || exit

if pgrep -u "$UID" -x 'quickshell|qs|hyprlock' | grep -qvxF "$1"; then
  exit 2
fi
